messages:
meera ops: Starting NYC1 GPU pool provisioning (8x A100-80GB nodes). Need a quick run of the validation checklist before handoff. Draft below — please run and post short results.

alex c: On it. I’ll run driver/kernel checks + smoke generation. ETA ~15m.

liam: I’ll validate VPC peering, SG rules, and egress path to object storage. Also checking quotas.

maria gonzalez: I’ll run a cost sanity check vs expected unit economics (batching on/off) and confirm reserved capacity tags for billing.

meera ops: Copying checklist (small, actionable):
```
1) Provisioning sanity
   - Instances healthy (node status Ready)
   - GPU visible via nvidia-smi on all nodes
   - Correct driver (>=525) and kernel module loaded
2) Networking
   - VPC peering routes in place, test s3/cos access from nodes
   - Security groups allow control-plane & telemetry (tcp 22, 443, 9090)
   - Cross-region fallback routes configured
3) Serving smoke tests
   - Start a sample model container (opt: compiled quantized variant)
   - Run 50 short requests, measure p95 latency and success rate
   - KV cache warmup check (repeat prefix requests, verify cache hits)
4) SLO gates
   - p95 latency < 150ms for short (32-token) requests under single-client load
   - Success rate >= 99.5% for generation requests (no crashes/500s)
   - GPU utilization stable and not throttling (no out-of-memory)
5) Observability & alerts
   - Logs flowing to central ELK/BigQuery; trace IDs present
   - Cost counters / token-metering enabled, per-model breakdown
   - Alerting: node-reboot, gpu-oom, high-latency firing tested
6) Security & compliance
   - KMS key accessible and rotation policy attached (if private slots)
   - Audit logs enabled + retention policy
7) Handoff
   - Documented runbook link in the cluster README
   - Handoff message to oncall with summary + links
```

alex c: Kernel/driver quick check done. All 8 nodes show:
```
Node node-nyc1-01 status: Ready
GPU 0: A100-80GB (driver 525.85)
... (8/8 nodes similar)
```
Result: PASS on visibility and driver. No mismatched kernels.

devops-bot: deployment-service: cluster-nyc1-gpu pool creation succeeded (job id f3c2).

liam: VPC peering validated. Routes exist: 10.40.0.0/16 -> cluster, NAT for egress present. S3 PUT/GET ok from a test pod. Security group note: control-plane health check requires 9000/tcp from ops subnet — had to add that.

maria gonzalez: Cost check: baseline per-hour estimate with current instance types = $16.4/hr/node. With batching (avg batch size=6) projected per-token cost down ~22%. Tagging applied: project:redwood-prod, env:nyc1.

alex c: Started serving smoke model (tiny-chat-8k-quant). Ran 50 requests: 49/50 success, 1 timeout (backend transient). Latencies:
```
median 28ms, p95 102ms, p99 190ms
```
KV cache warmup: second-run hit rate ~86% for repeated prefixes.

sre-oncall: p99 at 190ms is concerning but gate is p95 <150ms — p95=102ms passes. Need to test multi-client to ensure no regression under load. Also please note we require success rate >=99.5% (49/50 = 98%), that fails SLO gate.

meera ops: Noted on success rate. Alex, can you re-run the 50 reqs after increasing container concurrency to 8 and check logs for the timeout? Maybe transient throttling.

alex c: Re-ran with container concurrency 8, 100 requests: 100/100 success, p95 115ms, p99 175ms. Looks like the initial timeout was a transient network retry. Updated smoke result => PASS for success rate.

devops-bot: Monitoring rule test: high-latency alert (simulated) fired and routed to #incidents for smoke — OK.

liam: Latency SLOs look good for single-region. Verified egress bandwidth to artifact store stable at ~3.1 Gbps under load. No packet loss.

maria gonzalez: Confirmed billing keys and cost telemetry flowing. Added budget alert to trigger if burn rate > 1.5x forecast.

meera ops: Security items: KMS access verified for the private slots. Audit logs present in retention bucket (encrypted).

devops-bot: kubelet: detected GPU memory pressure on node-nyc1-04 during a heavy quantized compile job — OOM killer NOT triggered. Recorded metrics to /alerts/gpu-memory-pressure.

alex c: Investigated node-nyc1-04 compile job — it was an aggressive JIT compile from build pipeline. Throttled compile concurrency and retried, memory pressure cleared. Marking as INFO not blocking.

sre-oncall: For handoff we need a short readiness summary with these bullets: 1) SLO gates (p95, success rate) status; 2) Known issues (gpu-memory-pressure flagged but mitigated); 3) Cost/budget flags; 4) Runbook link + oncall contact.

meera ops: Drafting summary now. Will post readiness review invite for 10:30 PT and handoff to SRE if no objections.

liam: thumbs up from network side.

maria gonzalez: ack from finance side (budget alert set).

alex c: Ready to handoff, added smoke logs to cluster README: https://internal.redwood/nyc1/readme and uploaded model-latency traces to trace-ui.

meera ops: Handoff checklist complete. Marking cluster-nyc1 as READY_FOR_REVIEW and scheduling the brief readiness review. :white_check_mark:
